author.name: William Shakespeare
author.biography: Shakespeare left Stratford-upon-Avon for a career in London's theatres, where he worked as an actor, playwright and company shareholder. He knew stories as things people performed before other people, with attention, sympathy and judgment changing from moment to moment. Shakespeare's theatre could make a forest out of words and transform an actor before an audience's eyes. This comedy turns that power of make-believe towards the instability of desire.

hook.text: How much would you trust a love that changed overnight?

paragraphs: Several people enter a forest with firm ideas about whom they love. By morning, firmness will look less dependable.

In Athens, marriage is a matter of parental authority and social arrangement. In the woods, desire becomes subject to a different kind of interference. Shakespeare lets these worlds collide with a group of working people earnestly rehearsing a play. Their confidence in the power of theatre is both ridiculous and touching.

The comedy makes falling in love resemble a revelation and a mistake at once. A person can feel completely certain while being unable to explain why yesterday's certainty has vanished. Imagination supplies beauty; it also supplies evidence for what it wants.
Enjoy the transformations, then notice who has the power to impose them. How do we tell the discovery of a true feeling from an enchantment that happens to be persuasive?

orientation.text: Three groups cross in the forest: lovers, fairies and amateur actors. Keep their different projects in view as the plots begin interfering with one another.
